summary: Aleksandr Mikhailovich Osipov was a historian and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University (~1922–1926). He taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1926–1935), worked at the International Agrarian Institute (1932–1936), and chaired Indian History at Moscow State University (1936).

Aleksandr Semënovič Zimin was an Indologist who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy in 1920. He served as a Docent at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1934 and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 1937.
Aleksandr Vasil'yevich Popov specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kupiansk Theological Seminary (1871–1875) and under Vincenz Scherzl (~1875–1879).
Aleksandra Turek is an Indologist who completed her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Warsaw (1996–2009). In 2010, she became an assistant professor at the University of Warsaw.

Aleksei Davydovich Litman worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Moscow State University (~1945–1950). He served as Secretary at the Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan (1951–1956) and as naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957).

Aleksei Dyakov was an Indologist and historian who studied at Moscow State University (1913–1914, ~1916–1921) and Tomsk State University (1914–1919). In 1950, he became a professor at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Aleksei Osipovich Ivanovskii specialized in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1881 under Vasily Vasiliev, Aleksey Pozdneev, and Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (~1881–1885), later succeeding Sergey Georgiyevsky in 1894.

Indologist and linguist Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov studied at Kyiv University under Friedrich Knauer (~1910–1914), and under Sergey Oldenburg and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University (from 1922) and directed the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1938–1940, 1946–1952).

Aleksej Stepanovič Barhudarov, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1945–1950). He worked as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1953–1971) before joining the Institute of Linguistics in 1971.

Indologist Aleksey Sergeevich Sukhochev studied at Moscow State University (~1952–1957). In 1956, he took up a post as naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Aleksey Shakhmatov studied under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov and Theodor Korsch between approximately 1883 and 1887.

Alessandro Battistini is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He was a PhD candidate at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2014–2016), a Gonda fellow at IIAS (2016), a JSPS Fellow at Kyoto University (2017), and held a post at Bologna (2020).

Indologist Alessandro Giudice studied at the University of Pisa (MA 2020–2022) and University of Cagliari (PhD 2022–2026). He held posts at Pisa (2023), Cagliari (2025), Munich (2026), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at IKGA (attested 2022), and as assistant professor at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).
Alessandro Passi is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Pisa (attested 1993) and the University of Bologna (attested 1994–1995 and 2005–2007).
Alessandro Veniero, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, was a professor at the University of Catania in 1917 and served as principal at Liceo di Macerata from 1918 to 1919.

Alex McKay is a historian and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (ended 1995). He held research fellowships at SOAS, University College London, and the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Indologist and philosopher Alex Watson earned degrees from Oxford and SOAS, studying under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner. His posts include Wolfson College (attested 2006), Harvard (attested 2014), and Ashoka University (attested 2015–2025).

Alex Wayman worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning degrees at UCLA and UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau and Ferdinand Lessing. He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley (~1959–1961), Wisconsin–Madison (~1961–1966), and Columbia University (1966–1991).

Alexander B. Nicholson studied at Princeton Theological Seminary (B.A. 1864) and Government SPM Rajput College of Commerce. He became principal of Cedar Hill School (1876) before serving as lecturer and professor of Classics and Sanskrit at Queen's University of Ireland (1878–1902).
